w: Swamishri left Mumbai at 1.48 a.m. (IST) and reached Johannesburg at 10.24 a.m.(IST).

Swamishri and an entourage of 8 sadhus were welcomed in an evening assembly at the ‘Patidar Samaj Hall’. Swamishri, in his blessings, said, "... There are many philanthropists in this world. Some donate food, give employment, offer clothes as charity and give knowledge. Such charitable acts make us happy in this world but do not redeem us from dehbhav (body-consciousness) and bless us with atmabhav (atma-consciousness). A true sadhu dissolves the inner ignorance and enlightens us with the knowledge of God. He is the giver of the highest good. The holy sadhu helps us give up our base nature and bestow us with virtues. He remedies our diseased soul and that is why he is the greatest philanthropist..."

ph: Chanting the dhun as a prayer for rain

w: Swamishri performed the murti pratishtha of the marble murtis of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj, Radha Krishna Dev, Guru Parampara (canvas) and Hanumanji and Ganapatiji
16 July 200: (V.S. 2056, Ashadh Sud 15) Sunday, London, Guru Bhakti Din

The Redeeming Hand Prior to his morning puja, Swamishri was shown a small exhibition panel prepared by kishores and kishoris. Chirag briefly explained the panel and showed a card saying, "Swami, this is the hand of a kishore surrounded by a windstorm. Here, from the top is the outstretched hand of the Satpurush. It means that the kishore is in the midst of a storm of problems and worldly attractions and the Guru stretches his hand to redeem him." Swami stretched his hand and shook it with Chirag's , saying, "In this way you hold on to the Satpurush's hand." Vandan, a child, was standing nearby. Swamishri also shook his hands with him and said, "You too also hold on. Atleast you will not get strayed!" As Swamishri went ahead towards the mandir hall he saw a few youths. There too, Swamishri shook his hands with them. The Satpurush always lends his hand to support and redeem us.
Guru Bhakati Din To show their gratitude, love, and respect for Swamishri, all the devotees celebrated Guru Bhakti Din.

Through a dance and various speeches, balaks, kishores, and yuvaks highlighted Swamishri's qualities that make him a unique spiritual leader. In his blessings Swamishri mentioned the importance of maintaining good conduct in all aspects of life, since we are not here to put on an act, and our actions will speak for us. Earlier in the day, Swamishri had graced a special Medico-Spiritual Conference arranged for healthcare professionals. Sadhus discussed the crucial role spirituality plays in medicine, and Swamishri met all physicians present.
For the first time, all children of the Bochasan region gathered for Children’s Day Programme in the presence of Swamishri in Bochasan.
In the morning assembly, the children asked Swamishri some questions.
Question: How can we children become dear to Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj and you? Please teach us the method.

Answers: Becoming dear (to them) means they shower their love on us, call us, listen to us, they become like us and play with us. For this you have to please God and His sadhus. Study well, obey your parents, do not eat improper food, do not eat out, bow (daily) to your parents and guru. If you obey their wishes, you will become dear to them. 85Do not steal, do not tell ties. If you copy in school (the teacher) is not pleased. Similarly, if you steal even in the mandir, God is not pleased. Question: Please show us the key by which we can excel in studies and satsang.

Answers: To excel in studies go to school everyday. Whatever the teacher teaches, pay full attention and learn. But if you misbehave, you will not learn. Also, finish your homework daily. Whatever lessons have been given do them properly and do not watch TV. Only then can you excel in studies. The bad things shown on TV make bad impressions on your mind. So do not watch TV. If you have studied well, you can serve well, be of service to others and please God. Second, to progress in satsang, listen to spiritual discourses. Do not misbehave, since good devotees behave peacefully. Satsang is the sang (company) of that which is sat (truth) – that is God and His Sadhu. The scriptures are true, so by reading them, eg. Vachanamrut, Swamini Vato, one is said to be keeping their company. Dharma is sat, so by obeying the Shikshapatri God is pleased and dharma is strengthened. There are four things which are sat: God, scriptures revealed by God, the dharma given by God and the Satpurush. Also, the children of the Bochasan region asked Swamishri a written question: Swami Bapa, please write us a formula so that we may progress in every aspect of life.

In reply, Swamishri wrote: Offer bhajans (worship) to Bhagwan Swaminarayan. Develop unshakeable love, atmabuddhi, in the Satpurush. Pray. Keep faith. And concentrate/be focused. These are the ways to progress in life.
